desc:
Flutter feature development for existing apps means a new screen or a bug fix lands in your project the way your own team would have written it. Ecom Swift LLC builds on a branch, tests on iOS and Android and sends a pull request you can review.

## What is Flutter feature work?

Flutter feature work is paid development on an app that already exists. You send the repository and a brief, and a developer adds a screen, a flow or a fix without rebuilding anything around it. The goal is a change that fits your project, not a foreign island of code.

It is the right service when you do not need a whole new app, only one more thing: a settings page, a checkout step, a list that loads faster or a crash that has been annoying users.

## Why working inside an existing codebase takes care

Adding to someone else's app is harder than it looks. Every project has habits: how state is managed, how screens are named, where network calls live, how errors are shown. A change that ignores them works today and confuses the next developer tomorrow.

The common failure is a quick patch that introduces a second way of doing the same thing. A screen using Riverpod in a Provider app, or direct HTTP calls in a project with a repository layer, creates a maintenance bill that arrives months later. Reading first and matching the existing style is what prevents it.

## How this affects your product and your team

Good feature work saves your most limited resource, which is the attention of your core developers. They stay on the roadmap while the extra work happens on its own branch.

It also lowers risk. A change built on a separate branch, tested on both platforms and delivered as a pull request can be reviewed line by line, run in your own pipeline and rejected or adjusted before it touches the main line. Notes explaining what changed and why make the review faster, and make the change easy to understand later.

## What good Flutter feature delivery includes

- A written understanding of the brief, confirmed before work starts.
- A read through the relevant parts of your code, with your state management and folder structure followed.
- New screens built from your existing theme and shared widgets, so they look native to the app.
- Integration with your current API or data layer, not a parallel one.
- Sensible handling of loading, empty and error states.
- Testing on iOS and Android, on more than one OS version per platform in the larger packages.
- Widget tests or integration tests for new logic where the package includes them.
- Analytics events when you ask for them, using your existing tracking setup.
- A pull request with change notes, and release build help in the top package.

## How we work on your repository

We start by cloning the repository, building the app and running the existing tests, so we know the state we begin from. Then we plan the change, confirm it with you and create a branch.

We build the feature in small commits, run it on simulators and real devices, and fix what we find. When it is done, we open a pull request with a summary of what changed, which files are touched, how to test it and any decisions you should know about. Questions during review are answered quickly. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the size of the change, the amount of testing and whether we also help produce release builds. If an old Flutter version or a missing plugin makes a task larger than expected, we tell you before continuing.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Write the brief as a user story: who does what, and what should happen.
- Include designs, API documents or example responses if you have them.
- Tell us your Flutter version and whether the app currently builds cleanly.
- Name a person who can answer questions during the work.
- Review the pull request with your own tests and your own phone.

**Avoid:**
- Sending a vague wish and expecting the same result as a clear specification.
- Asking for a large change under a small package.
- Merging without running your own checks.
- Changing the scope in chat without confirming it in writing.
- Sharing your whole company account when a repository invitation is enough.

## Who this service is for

A startup whose one mobile developer is busy and needs extra hands for a defined task. A business owner whose original developer is gone and who needs a bug fixed before the next release. A product team that wants a new screen built to match its design system while it focuses on larger plans.

## What we need from you

Access to the repository as a collaborator, a short brief, and any design files or API documentation. If you use a private package source or a CI pipeline, tell us how it is set up. We never ask for passwords, and we do not need access to your store accounts for this service unless you want release build help. After you order, we confirm the brief and the branch plan before we write any code.
